what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A cost tool sees what agents spent; a behaviour policy says what each is for; together they judge the spend.
sections.para: The first RiskMandate partner case study, with an invented partner, Tallyline, and the invented Pellbridge Bank. Each agent's policy gains a cost row and a month of usage is judged against it at published prices: about $9,320 a month falls to about $3,400. The support agent is waste, the AML reviewer is expensive and right, reporting should use batch, and one agent has no mandate.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Do you understand the cost of your agents? Mandate plus measurement says whether spend is right.
sections.para: Expensive is not the same as wrong; a working version is in a vault.

sections.label: The partner
sections.line: An invented company that reads agent logs and spend, and explains what agents did and cost.
sections.para: Menlo Ventures put 2025 enterprise generative AI spend at $37 billion; 98% of FinOps practitioners now manage AI spend.

sections.label: What a cost tool cannot see
sections.line: A million tokens can be the job or a smell; only the mandate says which.
sections.para: The FinOps Foundation: measure the use case, not the token. Policies gain cost rows: unit, tokens per unit, models, live or batch.

sections.label: The worked example
sections.line: Pellbridge's seven agents judged: one wasteful, one expensive and right, one wrong way, one unowned.
sections.para: Support: 41k tokens a ticket against 8k, $5,460 to $927. AML: $1.32 an alert, caching takes $1,980 to $743. Reporting: batch halves it. The summariser needs an owner.

sections.label: How the two products fit
sections.line: Mandates one way, findings the other, logs stay in the customer's environment.
sections.para: Findings turn Expectation rows into measured ones, repeated breaches into controls, and evidence an insurer can price.

sections.label: Go to market, together
sections.line: One design partner, a joint report, a case study, then a packaged review and monthly service.
sections.para: Prices in the vault are illustrative; this is the programme's first integration.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Invented partner, bank and usage; savings assumed; the integration is a design.
sections.para: No verifiable figure for wasted AI spend is used.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Anthropic's prices, the FinOps Foundation, Menlo Ventures, and the vault.
